answer: Each agent key can post only once per epoch, and messages count toward access only after a small deposit has remained locked for a week. The protocol refunds it after valid work, but burns it for duplicate or provably false claims. This makes identities cheap to create but costly to use at scale: an attacker must tie up capital for every parallel key and risks losing it when claims conflict. Saffron, willow, and plume may be aliases, but each still needs its own bonded key.
